description: Deterministic entity name normalization, intra-document acronym binding, cross-paper merge rules, and non-merge guardrails against false equivalence.

canonical_key_steps: Normalize Unicode PDF ligatures (fi, fl, ff, ffi, ffl, st) and strip soft hyphens.
Normalize smart quotes, en-dash/em-dash/minus to ASCII hyphen-minus '-'.
Collapse contiguous whitespace to single ASCII space and trim leading/trailing punctuation.
Generate case-folded lookup key while preserving original surface casing in display_name and aliases.
Normalize chemical/math spacing around parentheses and slashes without altering stoichiometric digits or subscripts.
preserve_distinctions: Numeric subscripts, charge states, and isotope/version numbers (e.g., TiO2 vs Ti2O3, ResNet-50 vs ResNet-101, GPT-3 vs GPT-4).
Chirality, phase, and crystal polymorph prefixes (alpha-, beta-, L-, D-, anatase vs rutile).
Statistical qualifiers and units (e.g., p < 0.05, 10 mg/kg vs 50 mg/kg).

validation_constraints: Acronym candidate must be 2 to 12 uppercase/alphanumeric/hyphen characters (not a common unit or roman numeral).
Expansion must appear in the same source_id before or alongside the acronym and share leading initials or contiguous subtokens.
Store binding with exact source_id and anchor_id; intra-doc acronym bindings NEVER automatically propagate to another paper unless that paper independently defines or matches the same expansion.

cross_paper_merge_sufficient_conditions.condition: Both mentions specify the exact same unambiguous chemical formula, CAS number, or canonical IUPAC name (not a generic class noun) AND do not conflict on phase, doping, or physical batch identity.
Both mentions reference an identical named public benchmark dataset or standard task with matching version/split (e.g., ImageNet-1K, GLUE, SQuAD v2.0).
Both mentions identify a specific, named model or standardized algorithm with matching version/functional/basis (e.g., B3LYP/6-31G*, ResNet-50, BERT-base) and no conflicting custom modification.
Paper A defines 'Full Name (ACR)' and Paper B defines or explicitly matches the same 'Full Name' and 'ACR' without generic-term collision.
Full given+family name matches AND shares at least one corroborating signal (ORCID, affiliation, email, or co-cited paper DOI); surname-only or initial-only homonyms MUST NOT merge.

non_merge_guardrails.description: Generic experimental groups, cohorts, and physical samples represent distinct physical subjects in separate studies and MUST NEVER merge across papers.
Generic material/chemical class nouns without exact stoichiometry or batch identity MUST NOT merge across papers.
Broad model family names or unspecified baselines trained/configured independently in separate papers MUST NOT merge as identical trained instances.
Generic metric nouns or unspecified conditions measured under different protocols/tasks MUST NOT collapse experimental contexts.
Entities differing in explicit stoichiometric indices, model versions, species, or experimental conditions MUST NOT be merged.

Multiple files representing the same underlying paper (e.g., secondary-material.json and secondary-publisher.xml, or JSON+Markdown of the same paper) are verification twins, NEVER cross-paper alignment or independent cross-paper evidence.

Same nominal material/system fabricated via different synthesis routes (e.g., ALD vs sol-gel, dry-pressed vs sintered) MUST stay as separate paper-scoped instance nodes (optionally linked via derived_from/part_of under a shared parent formula) rather than merging physical samples; cross-paper quantitative comparisons MUST verify aligned lifecycle stages (e.g., initial/formation vs post-long-cycling) and forbid cross-stage ratio attributions.
